content:
I'd like to see oscillatory integrals in Mathlib eventually; as far as I'm aware there is nothing of the sort in Mathlib so far. Here is a project that I started: https://github.com/roos-j/lean-oscillatory
Working with my student Manasa Praveen, we've completed a very modest first goal, van der Corput's lemma on the real line.

There's a single file VanDerCorput.lean which contains 4 main theorems that should be exposed, and a few helper theorems that may or may not be useful.
I'm wondering where this could fit into the Mathlib hierarchy. Hopefully there will eventually be a lot of oscillatory integral stuff in Mathlib, so it might make sense to start a folder Analysis/OscillatoryIntegrals or similar?

Any comments and/or guidance welcome.

Btw. maybe I should say this to avoid confusion, there are various lemmas with labels involving van der Corput in the Carleson project; they're in a similar spirit, but different and adapted to the specific technical context needed there. The van der Corput lemma in this project is the standard textbook version. And then there is also (at least) one other famous lemma attributed to van der Corput, which number theorists will be familiar with..

I haven't written any code yet, but I was planning to define oscillatory integrals as (tempered) distributions. The thin that is missing is symbols classes and I am very unsure about how to define them properly to encompass all of the usual suspects

@Moritz Doll That would be great! Hopefully one day this can culminate in general FIO theory, which seems far away currently. My first goal is more elementary: prove the standard theorems about oscillatory integrals "of the first kind" in the sense of Stein, not the distributional sense (and symbol classes won't be needed at this stage).
